answer.why: CarGurus operates an online automotive marketplace where consumers research and shop for cars, and where dealers pay subscription fees for listings/advertising [T:P1.1–T:P1.5]. Cars.com is likewise a digital automotive marketplace that sells marketplace subscription advertising products to franchise and independent dealers, enabling them to showcase inventory to in-market car shoppers [C:S1.1, C:S2.1, C:S4.1]. Both share the same core product (online vehicle marketplace), the same paying customers (car dealers via subscription), the same free-side users (car shoppers), the same revenue model (dealer subscriptions + display advertising), and the same end market (automotive retail). The only modest differences are that CarGurus also operates a wholesale dealer-to-dealer platform (CarOffer) and serves Canada/UK in addition to the US, while Cars.com appears US-only — but these are minor deviations from an otherwise identical business model. These companies are direct competitors.

customer_segment.reason: Both sell to franchise and independent car dealers (B2B subscriptions) and serve car shoppers for free (B2C); identical dual-sided customer structure.

end_markets.reason: Both operate exclusively within automotive retail — new and used vehicle sales — with no meaningful divergence in end market.

business_model.reason: Both are two-sided marketplace/platform operators: free consumer-facing search funded by dealer subscriptions and advertising — the same fundamental operating model.

revenue_model.reason: Both earn revenue primarily through monthly dealer subscription packages for inventory listings, plus display advertising — structurally identical revenue streams.

value_chain_position.reason: Both sit between the dealer/automaker and the end consumer as intermediary marketplace platforms — same value-chain position.

geography_served.reason: Cars.com serves dealers and shoppers across the United States [C:S4.1]; CarGurus is #1 in the US but also operates in Canada and the UK. Mostly overlapping, with CarGurus having modest international scope.

specialization.reason: Both are automotive-only marketplaces with the same niche focus on vehicle discovery, dealer listings and consumer car shopping.

distribution_channels.reason: Both use direct sales teams to sell to dealers and automakers, and online/mobile platforms for consumer reach — identical channel mix.

regulatory_exposure.reason: Both face online advertising and consumer data privacy regulations (FTC, state laws). CarGurus also navigates dealer licensing and vehicle transaction rules given its instant cash offers, giving it slightly higher regulatory exposure.

C:S1.1.text: Cars.com is a digital marketplace and solutions provider for the automotive industry, connecting car shoppers with dealers. The Company sells marketplace subscription advertising products to dealer customers, enabling dealers to showcase their vehicle inventory to in-market car shoppers.

C:S2.1.text: Cars.com generates revenue primarily through the sale of online subscription advertising products to car dealer customers, which enable dealers access to their high-quality, in-market audience of car shoppers through vehicle inventory listings.

C:S3.1.text: Cars.com sells marketplace subscription advertising to dealer customers through varying packages, which allow dealers to showcase their available new and used vehicle inventory to an extensive audience of in-market car shoppers.

C:S4.1.text: Cars.com is a leading online automotive marketplace that connects car shoppers with dealers and private sellers. The company offers subscription advertising products and display advertising solutions to franchise and independent dealers across the United States.

C:S5.1.text: Cars.com provides digital marketplace solutions to automotive dealers, including marketplace subscription advertising, display advertising, and audience extension products. These products allow dealers and manufacturers to extend their reach on other advertising networks.
